newsitem.title: CHINA: China requires more details on listed firm reports.
newsitem.headline: China requires more details on listed firm reports.

text.p: China's top securities watchdog has ordered listed firms to provide more and fuller information in their annual reports for 1996 due for release by April 30, the Shanghai Securities News said on Friday.

The China Securities Regulatory Commission (CSRC) in a circular ordered that where auditors expressed reservations about the 1995 report of any firm, that firm must give details of measures taken during 1996 to resolve the differences.
If a company had a bonus issue last year, it must clearly state whether the money came from 1995 post-tax profits or from the firm's reserves, the circular said.
Companies listed in 1996 must report finance details of their initial public offerings, it said.
If auditors expressed reservations about a company's annual report for 1996, the firm's board must explain the differences at a shareholders' meeting sometime during 1997, the circular said.
